title: Tenant Network Change Authorization Matrix — PRD Draft
content:
Purpose and context
This doc is a working PRD for how Redwood should manage, authorize, and audit customer-managed network changes in Private deployments (VPC-connected and on-prem). It focuses on the authorization matrix, required evidence for approval gates, and corresponding audit log semantics. Current motivation: customers asking for clearer SLAs and security controls during network maintenance, tenant-driven config changes, and operator-assisted migrations. There have been multiple asks for predictable approval SLAs and tamper-evident logs tied to tickets.

Goals
- Define a minimal, enforceable authorization matrix for network configuration changes that balances customer autonomy with platform safety.
- Specify what audit events must be captured for compliance (who/what/when/why) and retention semantics.
- Design approval gate UX and automation for common change types (routing, firewall, BGP, peering, NAT, VPN).
- Provide a migration/rollout plan for existing Private customers.

Out of scope
- Deep vendor-specific device configuration formats (we will reference templates, not canonicalize per vendor).
- Full RBAC for non-network product areas (handled by console auth).

High-level change classifications (for gating)
- Informational: non-impacting metadata updates (labels, tags, contact emails). Minimal audit only; no approvals.
- Low-risk: idempotent config with immediate rollback (DNS TTL changes in a staging pool, tagging). Requires tenant-admin notification; platform operator optional.
- Medium-risk: changes affecting traffic flows but with automated rollback (ACL tweaks, route preference). Requires tenant sign-off + automatic pre-change simulation.
- High-risk: changes with potential tenant outage or cross-tenant blast radius (BGP origination changes, adding new peering, changing public NAT). Requires tenant admin approval + platform ops approval + scheduled maintenance window and runbook.

Actors and roles
- tenant-admin: customer user with network-admin privileges inside their Private deployment. Can request and approve tenant-scoped changes per the matrix.
- tenant-operator: customer network operator (may be script/service principal) that requests changes but cannot approve high-risk changes.
- redwood-platform-ops: Redwood on-call/ops staff with authority to approve platform-impacting changes and to execute emergency rollbacks.
- redwood-security: security reviewers who can block changes pending compliance review.
- integration-bot: automation that runs preflight checks, simulation, can auto-approve low-risk changes when checks pass.

Authorization matrix (text table)
Change type | Typical examples | Who can request | Who can approve | Preflight requirements | Audit evidence required
Informational | Labels, contact email | tenant-admin, tenant-operator | none (auto-apply) | none | event: user, time, diff
Low-risk | DNS TTL on internal pool, metadata | tenant-admin, tenant-operator | tenant-admin | automated sanity check | event: user, time, diff, preflight-check-id
Medium-risk | ACL rule updates, route preference | tenant-operator (request) or tenant-admin | tenant-admin (+ integration-bot signoff) | sim run with traffic model + mocked KV cache warmup | event: request-id, approver, sim-result, artifacts
High-risk | BGP origination, peering add/remove, NAT public IP swaps | tenant-operator request OR redwood-platform-ops | tenant-admin + redwood-platform-ops + redwood-security (if tagged) | scheduled window, runbook, rollback playbook, manual verification steps | event: request-id, approvers[], signed-runbook-ref, pre/post telemetry hashes

Audit log semantics
- Every change request must produce an immutable audit record containing: request_id, requesting_principal, requested_changeset (diff), risk_class, timestamps (requested_at, approved_at, executed_at), approvers list, linked_runbook (if applicable), preflight artifacts (simulation outputs), and execution logs (stdout/stderr and device responses).
- Retention: default 1 year hot, 7 years cold for enterprise customers on compliant tiers. Shorter retention (90 days) allowed for self-managed on-prem instances but must be configurable and documented.
- Tamper-evidence: logs must be signed or have append-only storage (customer chooses KMS-backed signature for private control plane). We recommend storing a hash chain checkpoint in customer KMS or Redwood-managed HSM depending on the deployment option.

Approval gate UX/automation (draft flow)
1) Request submission: tenant-operator or tenant-admin opens a change request via Console or API, attaching a YAML config snippet and a short justification. System generates a request-id and runs preflight checks.
2) Preflight: integration-bot runs static validation, simulation (traffic model), and kv-cache warmup estimation. Outcome recorded.
3) Notification: approvers are notified via console + email + optional Slack webhook.
4) Approval: approver approves via Console or an API call that must include a short approval comment and verification of at least one preflight artifact (sim checksum). Approvals are additive (e.g., both tenant-admin and platform-ops must approve for high-risk).
5) Execution window: for scheduled high-risk changes, the request is queued into a maintenance window with a start time. Execution logs are streamed and attached to the audit record.
6) Post-change verification: automated smoke tests run; results appended to audit. If any smoke test fails, an automatic rollback is triggered and recorded.

Edge cases and emergency handling
- Emergency override: Redwood platform-ops can perform emergency changes without tenant admin approval if there is an active incident affecting availability; such actions must be logged as 'emergency' with additional post-event review and mandatory notification to the tenant and security.
- Stale approvals: approvals older than configurable TTL (default 7 days for medium-risk, 30 days for high-risk) are rejected and require re-approval.
- Cross-tenant dependencies: where a change could affect multiple tenants (shared edge appliances), an explicit cross-tenant impact assessment is required and platform-ops must coordinate.

Telemetry, dashboards, and SLOs
- Console features: per-tenant change history, live execution logs, pending approvals dashboard, and per-change risk classification.
- SLO: approval notification delivered to default approvers within 2 minutes for auto-notify channels; manual approval turnaround targets are customer-configurable but we suggest 4 hours for medium-risk and 24 hours for high-risk for standard enterprise accounts.
- Alerts: failed preflight/sim must generate immediate platform-ops alert (pager) if it indicates possible regression or mismatch to baseline traffic models.

Migration and rollout plan
- Phase 0 (pilot): opt-in early customers, manual reviews by product + ops.
- Phase 1: automated preflight + tenant-admin approval workflow enabled for medium-risk.
- Phase 2: high-risk gate with dual approvers and scheduled windows; integration with customer KMS for audit signing.
- Phase 3: policy-as-code templates and self-service policy overrides for customers with dedicated contracts.

Security and compliance notes
- For customers requiring FedRAMP / ISO-like evidence, we will provide exportable signed audit bundles containing the complete chain: request, approvals, preflight artifacts, execution logs, and post-change telemetry.
- Least privilege: Console RBAC must minimize ability to request vs approve; we should avoid granting script principals approval rights.

Open questions / decisions needed
- Retention default: should platform default to 1 yr or 3 yr for all hosted Private customers? (Product + Legal decision)
- KMS-signing model: do we require customer-managed KMS as opt-in or enforce for enterprise tier?
- Simulation fidelity: acceptable thresholds for sim-pass — how do we quantify risk for ACL / BGP changes?

Next steps (short term)
- Sync with Security and Legal on retention and signing defaults (week of Jan 13).
- Build minimal preflight prototype for ACL updates and collect false-positive/negative rates (2-week spike).
- Prepare a pilot offer and invite 3 customers for Phase 0.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally prescriptive but also conservative — we want to be able to automate low-risk changes while preserving human oversight for anything that could cause tenant-visible outages.
- Please mark comments inline in the doc in Confluence PD-312 or drop notes in the linked Jira PD-4872.

Draft history
- 2025-01-10 Jordan K. initial outline
- 2025-01-20 Aisha P. added audit semantics and retention proposals
- 2025-01-27 Marco R. updated authorization matrix examples
- 2025-02-02 Lena Z. appended migration phases and open questions
summary: Draft PRD for an authorization matrix and audit semantics for tenant-managed network changes in Redwood Private deployments. Focuses on change classes, approval flows, audit requirements, telemetry, and migration plan.
